description: Day 2: with a real Vite dev server on the saved Pardner port, `pardner open` (with or without --http-port) fails with `INTERNAL_ERROR: Unexpected end of JSON input`. The person cannot tell that a port clash is the cause. Same root cause as F-007-01.
expected: PORT_IN_USE naming the port, and a working --http-port.
actual: Raw JSON-parse error; --http-port has no effect.

criterion: Flow economy: dead ends / data re-entry
description: The 60-second link lifetime is invisible: the CLI output for --output-file and the file itself say nothing about it, so an agent-to-human hand-off routinely fails and costs a full round trip (expired screen, Check again, ask agent again).
expected: The CLI result states `expiresInSeconds` and the signed-out notice states the lifetime; or a longer lifetime for --output-file links.
suggested_fix: Add expiry to the --output-file result and notice copy.

criterion: Same instruction worded the same everywhere
description: Four different wordings of "start Pardner" across surfaces: `pardner open` (startup shell), `pardner client open` (signed-out), "Check that it is still running" with no command (disconnected banner), `pardner open or pardner client serve` (CLIENT_NOT_RUNNING).

In WebKit (Safari, the macOS default the story uses) the Assigned to / Status filter / Vein selects render as small native controls (~24px tall with stepper arrows) next to 40px tab buttons; in Chromium they are styled 40px controls.
expected: Selects styled consistently across engines (appearance: none + custom chevron).
actual: Native compact selects in Safari only.
suggested_fix: Add `appearance: none` / `-webkit-appearance: none`, explicit height and a background chevron to the filter selects.
